approach.method_basis: The Parent searches a persistent tree of molecular graph edits. It starts from accepted molecules, buys scores directly at newly generated frontiers, and backs every real return up its exact route. Sibling molecular similarity shares observed peak returns for selection, while completed and pending visits control exploration and widening. After an observed strict incumbent improvement, it starts a fresh single-root episode at that accepted molecule, retaining the global accepted archive and bounded mutation/crossover generator.
approach.novelty: Add a certificate that a very specific branch has no remaining novel terminal: an ordinary neutral single-atom fluorine, chlorine or bromine whose entire reachable three-identity class has already received accepted scores in this session. Exclude only certified occurrences from live traversal and widening occupancy, preserving their stored returns and allocation counts so live ancestors can try other existing actions. This changes exhausted-support routing; the parallel siblings instead change root retention or deeper return sharing. It preserves the first observation of each class member and does not reuse the earlier broad size-floor rule.

observed_bottleneck: The actual code Parent n-e4b751133c75 successfully restarts direct-frontier tree search at accepted incumbents, but treats an exhausted finite action class as live search support. Its completed three-Search-seed mean is 0.49949631467224465 (available-seed SD 0.014066662744436314), +0.15139519654635733 over its own Parent n-85acb9fe7124 and 0.10753400153888635 below formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de. All fifteen summaries and run logs finish successfully, with 4,350 accepted optimizer proposals and no external invalid/duplicate proposals. A chronological replay of all fifteen session logs reproduces 19,286 outer graph actions, including 6,624 invalid actions. Exact singleton F/Cl/Br sources account for 14,486 actions in zaleplon_mpo Search seed 0 alone. Real accepted receipts already cover F, Br and Cl at optimizer indices 84, 87 and 112, respectively; 14,480 subsequent source-class actions produce 6,616 invalid results, 4,716 duplicate-child outcomes, 3,144 cycles/no-ops and four admitted aliases with no new molecular identity. The other fourteen sessions have zero exposure. Parent source proves all successful paths from an ordinary neutral member remain within these three identities. This is an eligibility defect after known support is exhausted, not evidence that small unscored molecules should be refused. The source proof is policy/scratch/r0055-01-improve-L01/source-proof.json, with the inherited source nodes/n-e4b751133c75/optimize.py; the exact exposed replay is policy/scratch/r0055-01-improve-L01/audit-seed-0-zaleplon_mpo.json with underlying nodes/n-e4b751133c75/seed-0/logs/zaleplon_mpo.log and nodes/n-e4b751133c75/seed-0/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl. All fifteen audit files, summaries, run logs and input hashes are enumerated in policy/scratch/r0055-01-improve-L01/evidence-manifest.json. The broader size-floor/closure admission pair n-19063a19f7ec activated but lost useful conversion, so it does not justify any general floor here.

hypothesis: Modify only active tree eligibility using C={F,Cl,Br}. closed(i) is true if and only if occurrence i has an exact canonical identity in C, its stored graph is the corresponding ordinary neutral single atom, and each identity in C has an actual accepted receipt in this Objective Session. Ordinary means exactly one atom, zero bonds, matching atomic number 9/17/35, zero formal charge/isotope/radicals/atom map/explicit H, nonaromatic, unspecified chirality, implicit H enabled and one total H, matching the checked round-trip graph for that canonical key. No score value, task identity, fixed evaluation index or rejection count enters this predicate. Under the unchanged operator menu replacement can only swap the other two halogens; append and fragment/crossover have no eligible attachment or cut, deletion has no legal atom, and insertion/bond/ring operations have no support. Thus accepted coverage of C certifies no novel reachable terminal, by induction over all successful paths. Remove exactly these occurrences from active child selection and its sibling-kernel support, and count only nonclosed children in widening occupancy. The widening threshold itself stays max(1,floor(1.5*(N+O+1)**0.5)). Refuse action attempts from closed sources before any RNG draw; allow the unchanged bounded controller to route to live ancestors/alternatives. Keep topology, all allocated-node capacity counts and exact N/W/O/M/receipt storage. Newly generated closed aliases may still be admitted from live sources under the unchanged admissions, but cannot subsequently become active support. This is one eligibility intervention, including its effect on kernel support and width occupancy; their individual effects are not separately identified.

finding_summary.headline: Certified pruning removes exhausted actions, but full and late gains and all fifteen endpoint scores stay unchanged.
finding_summary.insights:
This experiment separates a real computation bottleneck from the cause of the score plateau. Exhausted branches wasted substantial action effort, and removing that waste recovered live alternatives, but the paid proposal budget was already completed by the Parent. The exposed session still bought 170 proposals after activation without improving its incumbent. That makes insufficient remaining opportunity an inadequate explanation here; improving internal action efficiency alone was insufficient to improve the purchased search on this panel. Only one session exposed the predicate, so the evidence establishes a precise local efficiency benefit and no measured endpoint contribution under these conditions, not broad transfer or an end to the tree approach. Selection/kernel exclusion and widening changes remain a joint intervention whose separate effects were not isolated.

The method still has a proposal-quality limitation after the closed class is removed. In the exposed session, 167 evaluation positions changed but none of the later proposals beat the existing incumbent. Across the panel, proposals below six heavy atoms increased from 425 to 447 and those above fifty from 301 to 302, while nonempty typed scaffold coverage fell from 1,704 to 1,693 distinct scaffolds. Fragment-excluded within-session similarity changed only slightly, from 0.3888 to 0.3883 overall and from 0.4332 to 0.4315 late; this does not establish scaffold collapse. The Molecular assessment finds that useful ring, amino and carbonyl arrangements are reachable but are inconsistently preserved through graph changes, alongside reactive heteroatom linkages and unspecified stereochemistry. A proposal operator or search scheme that can preserve and recombine informative structural relationships could address this limitation; the present experiment does not test its utility or justify a general small-molecule ban. Wall time fell in the exposed session, but matching Parent suggestion timers and complete instrumentation overhead are absent, so the action-count result is stronger than a causal runtime claim.
finding_summary.results: The rule activated in one of fifteen sessions, after all three reachable halogen identities had been accepted and with 170 paid proposals still available. It eliminated all 14,480 post-certificate actions from that exhausted class, left the fourteen unexposed sessions exactly unchanged, and preserved the common prefix of the exposed session. Across all 4,350 paid proposals, outer actions fell from 19,286 to 4,842 and unproductive actions from 14,759 to 313. In the late half, the corresponding counts fell from 16,937 to 2,491 and from 14,645 to 197. Twelve widening decisions gained permission to expand live branches, and exclusions were associated with 84 actual paid outputs. None improved the incumbent; 43 distinct later descendants of newly widened routes also produced no gain. Full and late incumbent gains remained 4.365063 and 1.367463, with 148 and 42 improvements, respectively. Every task/seed endpoint stayed unchanged: mean 0.499496, a paired difference of zero and 0.107534 below the formal Anchor. Closure, accounting and efficiency checks pass, but both registered strict useful-conversion increases fail. The protocol verdict is refuted at that downstream layer, not a technical failure or a failure to execute the routing change.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic and amino chemistry persists, together with reactive linkages, size extremes and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: n-d2e77aeecb2f was inspected on the complete frozen Search panel: seeds 0, 1 and 2, all five objectives, 4500 accepted records including 4350 optimizer proposals. context.comparison reports both child_complete and paired_complete; published code Parent n-e4b751133c75 is the comparison. All 15 best-observed endpoints are identical to that Parent. Fourteen complete ordered SMILES/score sequences are identical; only seed-0 zaleplon_mpo differs, at 167 evaluation positions, first at evaluation 131. This is an output comparison, not an activation or component-contribution finding. The output covers fused aromatic heterocycles, saturated and bridged rings, amides, lactams, ethers, potentially basic amines, polyhalogenated frameworks and oxygen-rich acetals. The digest ring-closure rates are 0.8333, 0.8782, 0.8609, 0.8885 and 0.8402 in the frozen task order; aromatic-token rates are 0.7667, 0.8080, 0.8207, 0.8126 and 0.6828. These are string indicators, not fractions of atoms or measures of synthetic quality. RDKit inspection of the accepted optimizer trajectories finds 3742 molecules with rings and 3371 with aromatic rings, compared with Parent 3762 and 3396. There are 447 below-six-heavy-atom fragments and 302 above-fifty-heavy-atom structures, versus Parent 425 and 301. 842 proposals contain at least one N-F/N-Cl/N-Br/O-F/O-Cl/O-Br bond, versus Parent 820. These are structural flags, not measured instability. 2474 proposals have at least one RDKit-recognized unspecified tetrahedral centre, versus Parent 2466; all 4350 lack an explicit @ token. Global connectivity is diverse, while the best observed molecules within individual sessions often belong to a narrow related family. Common medicinal functional groups are reachable, but conventional synthesis, stereochemical definition and chemical stability are not established by validity or score. The digest final_molecules are last proposals, not final incumbents, and its initial excerpt is not the full pooled initial set. Evidence inventory and derived counts are in policy/scratch/r0055-01-improve-L01-molecular/inspection.json. Its per-cell audit files list each published Parent trajectory and a byte-identical run-local snapshot of the Child trajectory, with SHA256 hashes. Each audit explicitly preserves the original .worktrees/slot-1/runs/staging/seed-N/trajectories path supplied by the frozen request; snapshots are provenance copies, not published Child archives or an extension of SMILES citation authority. All trusted Child and published Parent trajectory paths existed when checked; no task, seed or Parent pairing is missing. No Confirmation or held-out evidence was inspected.

per_task.generated_character: The best observed molecules in seeds 0 and 1 are 24-heavy-atom, four-ring carboxamide-bearing fused frameworks with an ether bridge and fluorophenyl or fluorobenzyl substituent; seed 2 reaches a 25-heavy-atom, four-ring hydroxy/hydroxymethyl thione and N-N heterocycle. These combine recognizable functional groups with less routine fused-ring connections. The full 870 proposals range from 1 to 65 heavy atoms, with 123 below 6 and 16 above 50. Compared with Parent, this task alone changes its population: 123 versus 101 small fragments, 725 versus 745 ring-containing molecules, and 47 versus 25 molecules with the inspected heteroatom-halogen bonds. Seed 0 ends with the cited hydrazide/sulfonamide-containing 27-heavy-atom proposal at 0.1793142040128368, not a new incumbent.
liabilities: Small interhalogen, hypohalite and O-O/S-halogen fragments occur alongside chemically more substantial molecules.
Bridged ether geometries and the thione/N-N/hydroxy framework complicate synthetic plausibility; ring validity is not a synthesis route.
missing_features: Framework-preserving size and functional-group changes are inconsistent: many proposals lose the aromatic/polar organization present in the higher-scoring examples.
The best bridged and substituted saturated structures do not specify their tetrahedral stereochemistry; these records supply no preferred stereoisomer.
The observed ceiling does not identify an additional target-specific group that would improve it; a higher-scoring conventional alternative is not demonstrated.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The two carboxamide-bearing fused leaders score 0.42348216717712805; the seed-2 thione leader scores 0.4031937733859023. A more conventional quinoline/aryl-ether aminoketone at seed 0 evaluation 206 scores 0.40896418208928903. In contrast, Cl, OCl, OSCl and OOCl in the digest score 0.0. Within these observed structures the gradient favors substantial organized ring frameworks carrying polar functionality over isolated halogens and tiny heteroatom fragments. It does not establish one necessary scaffold, nor prove that the unusual bridges are beneficial. All three session-best molecules and their scores are unchanged from Parent.

per_task.generated_character: This unchanged Parent population is dominated by linked and fused aromatic heterocycles, ethers and halogenated substituents. The seed-1 best is a 33-heavy-atom, four-aromatic-ring polyaza/aryl-ether framework with methoxy, fluoroalkyl, aryl fluorines and an N-Br bond. Seed 0 instead reaches a 43-heavy-atom, seven-ring thione/thioether-rich assembly; seed 2 reaches a 31-heavy-atom, four-aromatic-ring pyrone-like carbonyl framework with amino, nitrile and aminomethoxy groups. The 870 proposals span 1 to 115 heavy atoms, including 74 below 6 and 133 above 50. Familiar ring and ether fragments coexist with large combinations and chemically questionable heteroatom substituents.
liabilities: The N-Br leader, peroxide-containing plateau examples and acyl-fluoride-bearing higher-score variants raise handling or stability questions not answered by the score.
Large linked aromatic/thione assemblies and strained ring products require synthesis assessment; no routes or material properties were measured.
missing_features: The sampled high-scoring family does not demonstrate a comparably scoring conventional replacement for its N-Br linkage while retaining its ring/linker arrangement.
Topology changes that preserve useful heteroaromatic organization without forming very large assemblies are inconsistent; the low-information plateau does not identify a missing target motif.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-1 leader scores 0.6354531001589825, while the distinct seed-0 and seed-2 leaders score 0.5852068576121547 and 0.581008100810081. Tiny or flexible examples CCOOC, COO, N#CCO and CCNC all score 0.5. The compact strained sulfone O=S1(=O)C2=CC(Cl)=CC21Cl scores 0.25043702473560003. The visible gradient distinguishes some richly connected heteroaromatic arrangements from a broad 0.5 plateau; it is not a monotonic reward for molecular size or simply having any ring. The N-Br-containing leader shows that the recorded score does not itself ensure conservative chemical bonding.

per_task.generated_character: The Parent-identical high-scoring output combines hydrophobic aromatic surfaces with amino functionality. The seed-1 leader has 28 heavy atoms and four rings, including two aromatic rings, a ring tertiary amine with a butyl substituent, an ether-linked N-C-O segment, methoxy and a halogenated diarylamine. Seed 0 reaches a 34-heavy-atom, five-ring amino alcohol with fluorinated aryl surfaces and an N-hydroxy saturated ring; seed 2 reaches a 29-heavy-atom, three-ring aminoalkyl/aniline/phenol/ether framework. The full population spans 1 to 92 heavy atoms, with 102 below 6 and 54 above 50 among 870 proposals. Many constituent motifs are ordinary medicinal chemistry, but the fused architecture and N-O or N-C-O chemistry keep synthesis and stability uncertain.
liabilities: Long alkyl, polyaromatic and polyhalogenated regions may complicate physicochemical behavior, which was not measured here.
N-hydroxy and N-C-O-containing ring arrangements and unspecified stereocentres remain chemical liabilities even in high-scoring examples.
missing_features: Potentially ionizable amines on ring and aminoalkyl frameworks are already reachable; the gap is consistent preservation of their relationship to aromatic surfaces during scaffold changes.
No defined stereoisomeric alternatives accompany the substituted saturated and bridged leaders, and protonation-state consequences cannot be read from the neutral SMILES or scalar scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-1 leader scores 0.9687642535682931; related fluoro-to-bromo and ether-to-thioether variants share that score. The seed-0 and seed-2 leaders score 0.9190747819767275 and 0.8602533326723711. The lower-scoring ketone/ether azaaromatic CCC(=O)CCCOCc1cc(C)nc2ccccc12 scores 0.0002220008414784072, and the N-sulfonyl cyclic amide example scores 0.0002562175393167918. The observed association is with the arrangement of amino and aromatic regions rather than mere nitrogen presence, halogenation or ring count. These scores provide no protonation, binding-pose or experimental activity evidence.

per_task.generated_character: This Parent-identical population retains aromatic, lactam/imide, ester/lactone and N-methylated heterocyclic frameworks. The seed-2 best has 34 heavy atoms and five rings, three aromatic, combining a phenyl-substituted N-N heterocycle, a larger N-methylated cyclic carbonyl framework, fused lactone and O-Cl substituent. Seed 1 instead reaches a 31-heavy-atom four-ring dicarbonyl framework with thioether and O-F groups. In seed 0 the best remains the supplied initial phenolic ester/phenyl/dicarbonyl heterocycle, also 31 heavy atoms; it must not be attributed to generation. The 870 optimizer proposals span 1 to 107 heavy atoms, with 71 below 6 and 74 above 50. Conventional carbonyl chemistry exists alongside hypohalites and enlarged fused-ring combinations.
liabilities: O-Cl and O-F are hypohalite linkages, not ordinary carbon-bound halogens; they appear in leading examples and merit explicit chemical scrutiny.
Enlarged cyclic carbonyl systems and stereochemically unspecified lactones may be difficult to realize selectively; scalar score is not synthetic feasibility.
missing_features: The output does not consistently retain the carbonyl/aromatic framework through size or topology changes, despite its association with higher scores.
A clean improvement over the provided carbonyl-rich starting framework is absent in one session, and the modest observed ceiling does not reveal a specific unobserved target substructure.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-2 leader scores 0.19720265943665388, the seed-1 leader 0.18484422002677828, and the retained seed-0 initial molecule 0.1678386594791329. A related methoxy-containing structure without the O-Cl group scores 0.19388096511675595; it is not a matched single-change experiment. S, O, C=N and N#CCCN score 0.0. The visible contrast favors organized carbonyl/nitrogen/aromatic frameworks over tiny fragments. Near-leading conventional ether chemistry shows that hypohalite functionality is not common to every high-scoring example; these observations do not isolate the contribution of any substituent.

per_task.generated_character: The unchanged Parent output has different compact N/O-rich families across seeds. The seed-0 best is a 25-heavy-atom, three-ring hydrazine/thiocarbonyl/N-N heterocycle linked to pyridyl and partially unsaturated N-fluorinated rings. Seed 1 reaches a 22-heavy-atom, two-ring aminoaromatic structure carrying an N-fluorinated four-membered N-N ring and O-N linkage. Seed 2 reaches a 24-heavy-atom, three-ring amino-acetal/azaaryl framework with hydroxymethyl, fluorinated side chain, bromine and chlorine. These are chemically substantial graphs, but N-F, crowded amino-acetal and strained heterocycle chemistry make synthesis and stability questionable. Among 870 proposals the heavy-atom range is 1 to 71, with 77 below 6 and 25 above 50.
liabilities: N-F, N-N, O-N and thiocarbonyl groups occur together in some leaders, while the acetal family is crowded and heavily halogenated.
Very large combinations add many functional groups without retaining the higher-scoring compact arrangement; zero-score examples are actual accepted proposals, not parser failures.
missing_features: The observed compact polar arrangements are not consistently available in conservative, less reactive scaffolds; high score alone does not validate the N-F or hydrazine/thione chemistry.
The substituted amino-acetal leader has multiple unspecified stereocentres; no stereochemically resolved alternatives are represented in the output.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-0 leader scores 0.4230032077811577, while its related phenolic pyridyl/thione precursor at evaluation 163 scores 0.37036805117359356. The seed-1 and seed-2 leaders score 0.35855114551835887 and 0.36108629330282105. The large acetal-rich combined structure at seed 0 evaluation 300 scores 0.0, as do several other large recombinations in the digest. The optimizer score median is 0.000042. The visible association favors certain compact polar and halogenated arrangements over bulky combinations, but does not identify N-F or any one heterocycle as necessary. Seed-2 evaluation 207 uses a fluoroalkyl side chain and scores 0.36108629330282105 versus the related evaluation-198 structure at 0.35490400735618427; this is a local observed comparison, not a general size or fluorination rule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-d2e77aeecb2f, frozen complete Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the same profile as published code Parent n-e4b751133c75. The 4350 optimizer records include 447 structures below six heavy atoms and 302 above fifty, versus Parent 425 and 301. High-score examples frequently retain linked or fused rings and polar groups, while cited tiny fragments or oversized combinations often score poorly; some small fragments instead occupy a nonzero plateau. Fourteen sessions are identical, so the aggregate structural change is concentrated in the remaining session. The evidence is an output association, not attribution to a search component.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve informative ring and polar-group organization while changing molecular size.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide task-agnostic contraction, expansion and rearrangement options that can preserve chemically meaningful ring and donor/acceptor relationships. Discover useful sizes through current-session accepted feedback; these records do not justify a universal size floor, ceiling or hard fragment ban.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-d2e77aeecb2f on the same complete frozen Search panel, compared with code Parent n-e4b751133c75. 842 of 4350 optimizer proposals contain an N-F/N-Cl/N-Br/O-F/O-Cl/O-Br bond, versus Parent 820. Leading molecules include N-Br, N-F, O-Cl and O-F examples; other high-score examples retain ordinary amide, ether or amino groups. A near-leading methoxy/carbonyl framework has no hypohalite. No stability, synthetic-route or matched substituent-contribution experiment accompanies these scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: High-scoring neighborhoods do not consistently furnish conventional alternatives to reactive heteroatom linkages.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expose chemically conservative bond, heteroatom and linker alternatives around accepted graphs while retaining their topological relationships, so those alternatives can compete using only session feedback. Do not convert this chemical concern into a claimed score benefit or an objective-specific motif recipe.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-d2e77aeecb2f, complete frozen Search panel and matched published Parent n-e4b751133c75. Higher-scoring observed molecules include ring tertiary amines, aminoalkyl aromatics, fused carboxamides and carbonyl-rich heterocycles. Lower-score examples can instead retain an aromatic ring or nitrogen in isolation without the same arrangement. The parent-identical sessions reproduce these associations, not independent confirmation or evidence that a single group explains the score.
transferable_gaps.gap: Aromatic surfaces and potentially ionizable or carbonyl-bearing polar groups are reachable but inconsistently retained together across scaffold edits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make chemically coherent changes of ring topology, saturation and linker geometry available while preserving useful local functional-group relationships when appropriate. Let accepted observations in each new session determine which relationships matter; do not import a named scaffold, prescribe a universal amine or use hidden identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-d2e77aeecb2f, the frozen digest and all accepted Search trajectories, with n-e4b751133c75 as published Parent. Every task has zero stereocentre-token rate, and all 4350 optimizer SMILES lack @. RDKit identifies at least one unspecified tetrahedral centre in 2474 proposals versus Parent 2466. The structures include amino alcohols, substituted acetals, lactones and bridged rings. These are representational observations; no stereoisomer-specific score benefit was measured.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not resolve stereochemical alternatives introduced by substituted saturated, acetal and bridged-ring chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Where supported by the identity and evaluation contract, preserve and distinguish chemically meaningful stereochemical states during graph transformation. Any utility would need to be learned from current-session accepted observations; the present evidence supplies no preferred configuration and no basis for claiming improved activity.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
